'''Thomas Muirhead Flett''' (28 July 1923 – 13 February 1976) was an English mathematician at [[University of Sheffield|Sheffield University]] working on [[mathematical analysis|analysis]].<ref name="Mathematics Genealogy Project">{{MathGenealogy|id=60910}}</ref><ref name="oxford journals" />

== Early life ==
Thomas Muirhead Flett was born on 28 July 1923, in [[London]], [[England]], when his parents moved from [[Scotland]] to [[London]]. At age 11, he won a [[scholarship]] by the County of [[Middlesex]]  from a state primary school to [[University College School]] (U.C.S.), Hampstead.<ref name="oxford journals">{{cite journal|last=Taylor|first=S.J.|date=1977|title=Thomas Muirhead Flett|journal=[[Bulletin of the London Mathematical Society]]|publisher=[[London Mathematical Society]]|volume=9|issue=3|pages= 330–339|issn=1469-2120|url=http://blms.oxfordjournals.org/content/9/3/330.extract#|doi=10.1112/blms/9.3.330|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Career ==
During [[World War II]], Flett was first employed as a laboratory assistant in the [[Post Office Research Station]] at [[Dollis Hill]], where the electronic computers used for code-breaking at [[Bletchley Park]] were being assembled.<ref name="oxford journals" /><ref name=wife/> While working, he studied part-time at Acton Technical College and obtained first class Honours in the [[University of London|London University]] B.Sc. general Degree in Mathematics and Physics. After working in the Post Office Research Station for three years, Flett worked as a research physicist at [[Simmonds Aerocessories]] in [[Brentford]] for two years. In 1945, pursuing his interest in Mathematics at [[Chelsea College of Arts|Chelsea Polytechnic]], he obtained class Honours in the B.Sc. Special Degree in Mathematics. In 1946, he obtained a mark in optional subjects, and in 1947, he was awarded for M.Sc. in Mathematics of London University.<ref name="oxford journals" />

After having received his early degrees as a part-time student, Flett entered [[Trinity College, Cambridge|Trinity College]] at the [[University of Cambridge]] in 1947. Under the guidance of Prof. [[John Edensor Littlewood]], he completed a Ph.D. degree in mathematics with a 1950 thesis entitled ''Some applications of estimates of exponential sums to the theory of functions''.<ref name="Mathematics Genealogy Project" /><ref name=wife/>

In 1950, Flett joined [[University of Liverpool|Liverpool University]] as a lecturer. While there, he authored the undergraduate textbook ''Mathematical Analysis: Theory, Methods, and Applications''.<ref name=wife/><ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=I3tfygAACAAJ |title=Mathematical Analysis: Theory, Methods, and Applications |first=T. M. |last=Flett |date=1966 |publisher=McGraw-Hill |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref> In 1966, Flett spent a year at the [[University of Washington]] in Seattle. In 1967, he joined the University of Sheffield as a professor of pure mathematics. Flett contracted [[multiple myeloma]]<ref name=wife/> and died in Sheffield on 13 February 1976 at the age of 52.<ref name="oxford journals" /><ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas Muirhead Flett |volume=3 |page=1315 |magazine=England & Wales, Civil Registration Death Index, 1916–2007}}</ref>

At the time of his death, Flett had almost completed his second textbook ''Differential Analysis: Differentiation, Differential Equations and Differential Inequalities''. It was edited and published by his colleague at Sheffield, Prof. John Sydney Pym.<ref name=wife/><ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UchPAQAAIAAJ |title=Differential Analysis: Differentiation, Differential Equations and Differential Inequalities |first=T. M. |last=Flett |date=1980 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0521224208 |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref>

== Family ==
In 1948, Flett married Joan Frances Ayers<ref name=wife/><ref>{{cite news |title=Thomas M Flett |volume=5f |page=542 |magazine=England & Wales, Civil Registration Marriage Index, 1916–2005}}</ref> (1923–2016).<ref>{{cite news |title=Joan F Ayers |volume=1d |page=688 |magazine=England & Wales, Civil Registration Birth Index, 1916–2007}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=MS Joan Frances Flett |magazine=England and Wales, Death Index, 1989–2024}}</ref> They had two daughters.<ref name=wife>{{cite web |url=https://sheffield.ac.uk/alumni/our-alumni/obituaries/tom-joan-flett-tribute |title=Joan Flett’s legacy in memory of her husband, Professor Tom Flett |publisher=University of Sheffield |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref>

Tom and Joan Flett were avid Scottish dancers. In 1964, they co-authored ''Traditional Dancing in Scotland''.<ref name=wife/> In 1996, Joan Flett updated their book as ''Traditional Step-dancing in Scotland''.<ref>{{cite book |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=is7fAAAAMAAJ |title=Traditional Step-dancing in Scotland |first1=J. F. |last1=Flett |first2=T. M. |last2=Flett |date=1996 |publisher=Scottish Cultural Press |isbn=978-1898218456 |access-date=28 October 2025}}</ref>
